name: Unsloth DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B (GGUF quant set)
license: Llama-3.1 Community License (quant repo: apache-2.0 tag)
notes: Not a distinct model - the repo's config.json is the base DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B config unchanged. It is recorded because the artefact people actually run is the quant set, and the file sizes are the serving budget. Measured sizes from the repo tree on the access date: BF16 16.07 GB, F16 16.07 GB, Q8_0 8.54 GB, Q6_K 6.60 GB, Q5_K_M 5.73 GB, Q4_K_M 4.92 GB, Q4_K_S 4.69 GB, Q4_0 4.68 GB, IQ4_XS 4.46 GB, Q3_K_M 4.02 GB, Q2_K 3.18 GB, IQ1_S 2.16 GB. The UD-* dynamic quants sit alongside: UD-Q2_K_XL 3.39 GB, UD-Q3_K_XL 4.20 GB, UD-Q4_K_XL 4.99 GB, UD-Q6_K_XL 7.33 GB, UD-IQ2_XXS 2.50 GB, UD-IQ1_S 2.16 GB. Counter-intuitively the UD-* dynamic quants are SLIGHTLY LARGER than the same-bit standard quants at this size rather than smaller: UD-Q2_K_XL 3.39 GB vs Q2_K 3.18 GB (+6.6%), UD-Q4_K_XL 4.99 GB vs Q4_K_M 4.92 GB (+1.4%), UD-IQ1_S 2.16 GB = IQ1_S 2.16 GB. That is the honest reading of the measured sizes: the dynamic recipe buys accuracy by keeping outlier tensors at higher precision and using larger group sizes, and at 8B those costs are not repaid by the bits saved on the bulk of the weights. The case for dynamic quants is at larger scale, where outliers are a bigger share - see unsloth-hermes-4-405b-gguf, where UD-IQ1_S is 87.22 GB for a 405.9B model. The load-bearing serving fact: an 8B reasoning distill runs in 3-5 GB at these quantisations, so resident KV and KV-cache type, not weights, set the batch size at long context - the repo README's own llama.cpp example passes --cache-type-k q8_0. imatrix_unsloth.dat in the repo root is the importance matrix used for calibration. KV bytes/token at bf16 (2 bytes/element): 32 layers x 8 KV heads x 128 head_dim x 2 (K and V) x 2 bytes = 131072 B/token = 128.0 KiB/token. bf16 KV is 16.00 GiB per sequence at 128k, 3.3x the size of the 4.92 GB Q4_K_M weights. context_scaling is null: context length is native to the pretrained config, no rope_scaling.
